raw_response:
My land is 12.4 mu, and cotton is my main crop like most people around here in Quzhou. I've been doing this 30 years so I know what works on my soil. Let me think it through.

Cotton is my biggest piece — I'll put about 9 mu in cotton this year, same as last year. The price has been okay and I know the crop. I'll buy hybrid Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town, that's what everyone uses now because of bollworm. For fertilizer on cotton, I put down a compound fertilizer (45%, 15-15-15) as base, about 50 kg per mu, then urea topdressing at flowering and boll-setting. That gives me around 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K per mu. Cotton is hungry for nitrogen but I don't want too much or it grows tall with no bolls. Water from my well 3-4 times through the season. Pesticide — cotton needs a lot. Aphids early, then bollworm, mites, maybe whitefly. I spray 6-7 times usually. Rotary till before planting.

Then I have 2 mu of wheat-maize rotation on my better soil. Wheat in October after maize harvest, then summer maize after wheat in June. For wheat I use an improved variety, about 12 kg N, 6 kg P, 5 kg K per mu, irrigate 3 times including the spring green-up water. Expect around 450 kg per mu. For summer maize I use hybrid Zhengdan or similar, 15 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K, irrigate twice, no-till direct seed into wheat stubble since that saves time and diesel. Maize around 500 kg per mu.

Peanut on 0.8 mu — my wife handles that mostly, for household oil and some sale. Improved variety, light on N because peanut fixes nitrogen itself, more P and K. Plough the peanut ground because it needs loose soil.

Mung bean on 0.6 mu, traditional seed saved from last year, almost no fertilizer, one pesticide spray maybe. It's for family eating and a little extra.

My total fertilizer cost is the big expense. I'd rather put a little extra than come up short — a bad harvest hurts much more than some wasted urea.
